summary: Redwood hosted embeddings + reranker walkthrough for MerchantWave search refinement. Covered embedding endpoint choices, vector DB vs Redwood hosted flow, reranker endpoint for recall->precision tuning, console metrics, cost/latency tradeoffs, and security questions (VPC, KMS, SOC2). Agreed next steps: run a 1-week pilot benchmark and share security docs.
topics: security: VPC/private deployment, KMS, audit logs
transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — I'm Maya from Redwood. Omar is with me for the demo. how are you all?
[00:06] Daniel: Doing well, thanks. We are excited — searching is our pain point right now.
[00:10] Priya: hi, sorry for the delay, just pulled in the query logs.
[00:14] Maya: no worries. Quick agenda: embeddings endpoint, how you'd wire it to your vector store, then our reranker endpoint and the console/Optimize suggested knobs. We'll keep it interactive.
[00:28] Omar: quick intro — I'm Omar, solutions engineer. I'll show live calls to the hosted embeddings and rerank endpoints and some perf numbers.
[00:36] Carlos: great. high level we want to reduce false positives on product search, so hopefully the reranker can help bump relevant items. Also worried about cost at scale.
[00:46] Maya: totally, and we can talk about batching + caching to control token costs.
[00:52] [01:00] Omar: okay pulling up the sample app — note this is connected to Redwood's hosted embeddings endpoint. First step: we create embeddings for titles and descriptions. We recommend embedding the title + a short context field, not whole product copy, unless you need generative context.
[01:18] Priya: for us most items have long descriptions, is there a token threshold you'd recommend?
[01:22] Omar: yeah try to keep pieces under 512 tokens for better cosine behavior. You can chunk long descriptions and index as multiple vectors, then reassemble. There is some loss tradeoff but it's workable.
[01:33] [01:40] Omar: now I'm running a top-k nearest neighbor query against their vector store (we demo with an in-memory mock). you get X candidates. those go into the reranker endpoint — a lightweight neural rerank model that takes the query, candidate ids, and returns a score.
[01:55] Daniel: is the reranker hosted in Redwood or do we host the weights?
[01:58] Omar: hosted — it's a managed endpoint. we support pinning specific reranker model versions for reproducibility and rollouts. For private deployments you can also run the reranker inside your VPC.
[02:08] Priya: latency concern — our SLA is 200ms p95 for search. can you hit that with rerank?
[02:12] Omar: depends on candidate count. If you pass top-50 and do batch scoring, we've seen median ~80-120ms and p95 in the low 200ms on hosted single-region configs. With Dedicated capacity you can drop that p95 by ~30-40ms. Also kv/prefix caching helps if repeated queries.
[02:30] Carlos: curious about cost math — embedding + vector store + rerank — what's typical?
[02:36] Maya: rough rule of thumb: embeddings per doc + vector DB ops are main cost for indexing; inference cost for reranker depends on how many candidates you score and the model size. Omar will share a mini-benchmark sheet.
[02:46] [03:00] Omar: demo time — hitting /v1/embeddings with a sample payload. note we have model variants tuned for cheaper 8-bit quantized embedding vectors vs high-dim ones for quality. sending now... response looks like a 768-d embedding.
[03:18] Priya: are these deterministic? we need stable vectors for reindexing.
[03:22] Omar: stable per model version; if you change model or quantization profile you'll see drift — which is why we recommend pinning model versions and using Redwood Console's model rollout to orchestrate migrations.
[03:34] [03:40] Omar: next I call the rerank endpoint with query + candidate ids. the body is small, response gives scores and a short feature attribution string. note: feature attribution can be noisy — it's heuristic.
[03:52] Daniel: feature attribution would be very helpful for product teams to understand why something bubbled up.
[03:56] Omar: we agree — think of it as a triage signal not absolute truth.
[04:02] [04:20] Priya: about the vector DB — we're currently on Pinecone. what's the value prop to move to Redwood-hosted vectors?
[04:27] Maya: you can keep Pinecone — Redwood plays well with external vector stores. The hosted flow simplifies ops (no separate infra), gives integrated rollouts and cost telemetry per route in Console, and prefix/KV caching which can reduce DB calls. If you need full control, Dedicated or Private keeps everything in your VPC.
[04:46] Carlos: So we could keep Pinecone for large product corpora and use Redwood reranker?
[04:49] Omar: yes, that hybrid is common — recall from your vector DB, rerank in Redwood.
[04:54] [05:10] Daniel: security — we need SSO + SAML, audit logs, SOC2, and KMS for keys. do you have those?
[05:16] Maya: yes SOC2, SSO via SAML/SCIM, RBAC in Console, and Redwood integrates with customer KMS for private deployments. We'll send the compliance pack.
[05:26] Priya: for Private, does the inference plane sit in our VPC?
[05:29] Omar: yes for Private the control plane is customer-managed and inference nodes can be in your VPC; for hosted we have encryption-in-transit and at-rest and you can use SSE with our managed keys or bring your own in Dedicated.
[05:42] [06:00] Omar: switching to Console — here's the per-route latency breakdown, cost-per-token, token counts, and error traces. you can set a rollout policy with automatic fallback to a smaller model if latency exceeds threshold.
[06:16] Carlos: that's appealing — our product team wants fine-grained rollout knobs.
[06:20] Omar: also Optimize will suggest batching sizes and a quantization profile based on observed traffic. we had a customer cut token spend 28% by following those suggestions.
[06:33] [07:00] Priya: whats the retry strategy if reranker fails? we can't have whole search break.
[07:05] Omar: default is graceful degradation: if reranker times out we fall back to the original vector ranking. you can configure thresholds and canily/canary percent for rollouts.
[07:18] Daniel: can we shadow traffic to test a model?
[07:21] Omar: yes, Console supports shadowing and A/B with traffic splits.
[07:27] [07:45] Maya: quick note on evaluation — we recommend a labeled dataset of queries with relevance judgments. Redwood can host the evaluation harness and alert on regressions per rollout.
[07:55] Priya: we have a small set of labeled queries — would you want that for the pilot?
[07:58] Maya: definitely. share them and Omar will run a bench.
[08:05] [08:20] Omar: okay running a small candidate set now — we'll time it. sending top-20 -> rerank. response 138ms median in this demo env. note this is non-prod.
[08:35] Daniel: good to know. what about scaling — if we have spikes from sale events?
[08:40] Omar: autoscaling for hosted works but you can also provision Dedicated pools with burst capacity. you can set SLO-based routing that routes lower tier traffic to cheaper models.
[08:54] Carlos: do you expose per-token cost per model in the console?
[08:58] Omar: yes, cost per token and per-route aggregated. you'll see cost broken down by embeddings vs rerank vs generation.
[09:10] [09:30] Priya: any setup complexity — SDKs, auth, sample code?
[09:33] Maya: we have SDKs in Python/Node, curl examples in docs, and quickstart template for embeddings + rerank. We'll share a GitHub repo link.
[09:46] [10:00] Daniel: what's the expected timeline for a pilot? we want to test on a subset (10k SKUs) for a week.
[10:06] Maya: doable — typical pilot is 1 week of traffic capture + bench. Omar will deliver the mini-benchmark script you can run in your infra.
[10:12] Priya: ok send estimate for cost of pilot and potential Dedicated pricing if we like results.
[10:16] Maya: yes, we'll include both hosted pilot cost and a 3-month Dedicated ballpark.
[10:23] [10:50] Omar: final quick notes: use top-k=100 for recall-heavy queries then rerank top-50 to tradeoff cost/latency; enable prefix caching for repeated queries; use Optimize suggestions after 48 hours of traffic to tune batching.
[11:06] Carlos: thanks — that was very practical.
[11:10] Maya: any other questions?
[11:14] Daniel: not right now. we'll expect the benchmark and security pack.
[11:18] Maya: great — we'll follow up with links: deck https://redwood.example/decks/mw-search-playbook, repo https://github.com/redwood-inference/merchantwave-onramp, and the security pack doc. Thanks everyone.
[11:30] (call ends)
